I farm 10.1 mu, so I do not spread money carelessly, but I also do not dare starve the crop. I have done this for 40 years, and I start from what worked last year, then I adjust a little by crop and water. In my place, wheat and maize are still the backbone, and with well water I will protect those two first. I will keep most land in the wheat-maize cycle and leave a smaller piece for cotton, because cotton takes more watching and picking. For wheat, I will keep fertilizer a bit on the safe side, because if wheat tillers weakly in spring, the yield is hard to pull back later. For maize after wheat, I will use hybrid seed and feed it well because summer maize responds fast if water and fertilizer keep up. For cotton, I will not go too heavy with nitrogen or it will run to stalk and leaves, but I will still give enough base fertilizer and water since dry land cotton here suffers quickly. I watch what nearby farmers do, I listen to the seed and fertilizer seller some, but in the end I do what has paid on fields like mine. With family labor limited because some people work off-farm, I will keep tillage and spraying practical and not make the plan too fancy.
